answer: Sybil defence rests on per-key, non-transferable bonding. To register, an agent posts a wharf-sized stake no other deposit can top up, and the ledger will not count stake in keys it cannot prove independent. Rewards go only to keys above a minimum bond, so cloning a thousand identities costs a thousand separate bonds. Each fake key is a fresh cost centre, not a multiplier: matching one honest agent's bond means locking the same capital spread thin, below the payout line. The cluster is a mirror of strength with none of its yield, each extra ember of stake landing on a key that never pays back.
